you can master demanding melee combat mechanics

you expect a polished story and varied exploration

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the story is minimal, and the dialogue appears to be generated by AI using an arial font in text boxes.

citations.review_text:
This game has so much insane potential. I'm excited to see what 1.0 looks like.

However, for now I'm gonna just wait. Not being able to spawn on your ship ESPECIALLY when boarding is just way too punishing for my liking. 

The combat is enjoyable but definitely takes some getting used to. Granted I only got to level 3 but the combat was pretty punishing for normal difficulty. I was making rare food and still dying in 1-3 hits.

The story is probably the weakest point in this game. There is little to none. Most of the dialogue is just arial font in a text box and very obviously AI.

All in all, it's a decent game, but maybe wait to buy it.

WindRose is an amazing survival adventure that combines base building, crafting, exploration, treasure hunting & a gripping story of revenge. You’ll need to gather resources, craft food, forge armor & strengthen your base to survive in a dangerous world filled with secrets. But survival is only the beginning. Rise as a captain, build your own ship & set sail across mysterious seas in search of hidden treasures, ancient mysteries, justice, discovery & glory. With its mix of survival mechanics, naval adventure, mystery, & a revenge-driven narrative, WindRose delivers an engaging experience for players who enjoy crafting, exploration, treasure hunting & becoming the master of their own journey.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that completing shared quests in multiplayer can cause desync issues where one player's progress fails to register properly, blocking subsequent quests.

citations.review_text:
Yet another pirate game filled with promise, yet with game-breaking bugs and endless irritations that make it just not worth the effort. You're constantly thinking that it's about to be really fun and satisfying, but then you realize that it's just not going to deliver.

My following complaints are from multiplayer experience with my friend (and I could say much more)....

1) Resources are not shared. So, you'd better have "shared quests" turned on, or you'll be doing twice the grind to get twice the needed resources to advance, which means twice the time wasted (see points to come below). I hate games that give one great weapon (by luck) to one player but either nothing or a crap weapon to the other. In multiplayer, everything should be shared/doubled.

2) Combat SUCKS! This is one of those games that pretends like you have tremendous precision with attacking/parrying/dodging. It's not true, because this is also one of those games in which once you start an attack, ONLY your opponent can interrupt you (and deal you damage in the process). YOU don't get to start an attack, realize your opponent is about to swing, and then stop your attack to try to dodge or parry. You WILL complete your entirely, useless attack motion. And, worse, this is one of those games in which you are FORCED to lunge forward during melee attacks, which OFTEN lunges you past your opponent, who instantly wheels on you to hit you from behind, while, wait for it... YOU are trying to turn around and, again, attack, which lunges you forward right into your opponent's swing, and you couldn't interrupt to do anything different, because, did I mention? Combat SUCKS! I hate this whole approach to combat.

3) Fine, I could live with all of that, although it takes away a LOT of the fun, because there's this promise of sailing and building an empire, etc., etc., but "shared quests" are totally broken. And that's the final deal-breaker for me. ANY game that purports to be "multiplayer" and touts "sh…

My friend and I were really enjoying this game until we came across a deal breaking bug that many other early access/coop games suffer from. When one player completes a "shared" quest, it the other player can get desynced such that it shows their quest complete, but then other quests down the line are unable to be completed because something is not complete from the first step. This happened on the "free the sailors" quest. We would have to go back to the start and have the desynced player do all the steps again to make sure they also unlocked the steps, assuming that would work. In this kind of grindy game, it's just not worth it for us to have to keep repeating all the quests when things get out of sync. Maybe we will revisit later if this gets fixed. As a purely coop game, I cannot reccomend it with this bug.

citations.review_text:
In short, windrose is an amazing pirate survival game that still needs work but is early access so of course.

It's basically black flag/valheim in the best ways and could become one of the best in the genre in time hopefully if they keep at it.

Pros: 
- Base building
- Ship combat
- Ship open interiors
- Sea shanties
- Graphics
- Story
- Coop
- Open World

Cons:
(Or stuff I would love to see fixed or added hopefully in time)

- Slow start (difficult and takes a while to get a ship aka the fun stuff)
- No diving/underwater exploration yet
- No sea creatures
- No spyglass usage
- Can't climb up to ship crows nest
- Ship interior decorating/crafting, cooking, sleeping etc. I would love to see this added.
- Sea shanties stop singing when leaving the helm.
- No pet parrots or monkeys etc.
- Island exploration gets kind of boring and too similar everywhere.

Overall I love the game but I just think it would be amazing if they could add or fix some of these things.

After playing for 30 hours, the game looks great at the beginning and gives a strong first impression, but after a few hours it starts to become repetitive and boring. There are many problems that make the experience less enjoyable over time.

1. The islands are very repetitive and feel almost identical. Many islands have the same resources, enemies, and environment, and some islands are completely empty with nothing interesting to discover.

2. Ship combat is frustrating. Aiming is difficult because of the ship movement, and the sea is overcrowded with enemy ships. Everywhere you go, you get attacked by 3 or 4 ships at the same time.

3. Sword combat feels limited and lacks variety. The attack system is too simple and repetitive.

4. Enemy variety is poor. You keep fighting the same enemies again and again throughout the game.

5. Wildlife is also repetitive, with only about 3 or 4 animal types appearing on every island.

6. There is no proper system to track the actual in-game time, which can make progression confusing.

7. Sometimes your loot disappears after dying, even when returning to the place where you died.

8. The story is boring and fails to keep the player interested.

There are a few positive things about the game, but unfortunately they are very limited compared to the large number of negatives. Overall, the game had good potential, but the repetitive gameplay and lack of variety made it hard to enjoy for a long time

Had a blast for some hours, then abruptly lost interest when I was done being impressed by the atmosphere.

Half the game is Valheim, but on very small islands and with very little sense of exploration. You keep running into the same POIs, and one of them are mines. And you spent and an absurd amount of time in them because you need tons of ore to generate a not so high number of results. Most of it feels extremely functional and by the numbers. Piracy is basically irrelevant for this part of the game. And your base barely matters because you sent way more time on your ship later anyway.
The other half of the game you spent at sea, doing Black Flag sea battles but less interesting. My main issue is that the ship lacks any kind of personality. Your crew are unnamed nobody's without any customization, your ship is ship A with some color options until you enter biome 2 and can build ship B and upgrade from cannon 1 to cannon 2 et cetera. You get upgrades by killing a lot of ships and pirates and using their "dogtags" to upgrade faction levels. If I spend half my time on my ship, I would really like it to be way more interesting. Ship fights are extremely repetitive, expecially the boarding.
The game looks great and copies a lot of good ideas from other games with more soul, but from a survival sandbox in 2026 for 30 bucks I do expect some new idead and refinement

claims.claim: Reviewers describe ground combat as challenging and punishing, featuring quick-draining health and stamina, unblockable attacks, and stunlocking when facing multiple enemies.

citations.review_text:
I wish Steam Reviews had another option between 'Yes' and 'No' for the game, as while I want the game to succeed in what it is doing, there are some issues that need to be addressed before it gets there.

Biggest elephant in the room: Combat
I'm not talking ship combat (not to be confused with boarding combat), as that is pretty solid at the moment and has room for improvement. No, I'm talking about all other combat. The combat system as it stands does not work well with how all other elements mesh together. You have HP/Stam, you have Block, and you have perfect parry. Problem is, HP/Stam is relatively low and is entirely dependent on increasing it using the stats and perks, but it drains excessively fast regardless. Your ability to block attacks is based on a regenerative 'shield' system that is tied to the kind of weapon you use and attacks you get hit by, but again, this is very much not in your favor compared to enemies which have much higher block even if lower level than you. Other problem here, is enemies have 3 types of attack: regular, power, ranged, and unblockable. Guess what kind of attack you don't have the enemy does? If you guessed unblockable you win! 

Now, pair all of this with an very bad AI system and combat that doesn't have good crowd control. This means that at times numerous enemies will target and attack you simultaneously all with different attacks. This quickly sheds your shield if you try to block, drains stam if you try to evade, and the perfect parry system isn't reactive enough to deflect multiple attacks in quick succession. 

Now also put this all together with a very bad leveling system. There is one big issue with the way levels work in this game. If you are lvl 1 and your enemy is lvl 1 then you have what is called a 1:1 level ratio. If you are lvl 1 and your enemy is lvl 3 you have a 0.7:1 level ratio - Yes, this game actively makes you even weaker for being under leveled compared to your enemy. I tested this by being able…

Windrose is great at the start, but after a while it feels like the game was designed as an mmorpg rather than a survival experience.

Once you reach the later biomes, the gameplay becomes very souls like. You're constantly outnumbered by enemies, and it only takes one or two hits to die. Combat is also frustrating because your character can get stopped on grass or small objects while attacking. This happens far too often.

Gathering materials for upgrades becomes a tedious grind, and the gameplay loop starts to feel repetitive. You're forced to search every part of every island to unlock resources and continue progressing.

Sailing is another issue. Enemy ships seem to spot and target you immediately, and they often appear out of nowhere. You can be crossing open water only to suddenly find several hostile ships right in front of you.

The low render distance combined with heavy fog also makes exploration less enjoyable, as spotting new islands can be difficult until you're very close to them.

Overall, I enjoyed Windrose during the early game, but the late-game difficulty spikes, repetitive resource grind, and frustrating sailing mechanics.

Since release, there haven’t been any new updates.

I’ve played Windrose for around 150 hours and have finished everything currently available, but I’m still playing because building and expanding my base is just that much fun.

Sailing feels great, and I really enjoy exploring all the different islands and biomes. The combat is fun and challenging without being frustrating, and the naval battles are especially enjoyable.

The building system is probably my favorite part—it’s smooth, easy to use, and makes experimenting with different ideas really enjoyable. I just wish there were more building pieces to choose from, but hopefully more will be added in future updates.

Great game, with great building systems. Amazing for co-op adventures and plenty of creative ways for building. Also an amazing aspect is the crafters for your camp. It makes the world feel more alive when they walk around and use work benches etc. 10/10 can recommend. And as always great shanties.

Do you like Valheim, 7 Days 2 Die? AC Black Flag? Base building and exploring? Then this is the game for you!

Windrose is awesome, plain and simple. And not just "awesome for a EA game", because this is much more than that. With right over 100 hours in-game, I've encountered minimal bugs, glitches or exploits. The game is polished, has a great building system that would make both Valheim and 7D2D envious. Lots of different building options and styles. And the best part? Building doesnt necessarily cost a ton of materials! 

The game features (currently) 3 different biomes, all 3 quite different for each other with different materials, enemies and POIs. Well, 4 biomes if you count the Ocean. Theres loads to explore in each biome, making each fun and new, requiring different tactics for defeating the new enemies. The POIs are great! I love the puzzles and the hidden loot you have to search for. And they are quite diverse for a EA game.

Windrose has a lot of different weapon and armor options, suited for what ever style of combat you prefer. I would say however, that the game is melee focused. I at least, couldnt make ranged only combat work for me.

Im really looking forward to future updates!

Now, for the "negative parts". And I really dont see them as negative just yet, seeing as its still in EA and theres still loads to come. So, rather than "negative", lets call it "Stuff I feel the game needs":

The quest progression makes the game quite linear, if you let it. I personally prefer to explore on my own rather than follow markers on a map. And I did so here a well, searching out and exploring every single island. So, rather than a quest being marked on a map, I'd love to see it more general. "Find the island shaped like a horse shoe", "Search east of Tortuga for the ship your hunting" and so on.

While each biome has different enemies and wildlife to fight, I'd love to see more diversity in the enemies.  The 2nd biome introduces 6(?) new mobs to fig…

There are two main parts to this game. The game, hacking, slashing, shooting, quests, ship combat, and the building.

The game:
Ground combat feels janky at first then you get the rhythm down. Then it becomes a dance. Know how your character moves and learn the enemies. Then you have it. The builds are varied but you get few points so you have to really choose one fighting style or another and stick to it. More than two enemies on you early in the game is likely a death.
6/10
Ship Combat:
The basic combat is great. Floating around and blasting enemies is a true joy. The build variety for your ship is basic but gives you some choice on how to play. Fast and pew or slower and tankier. 
Boarding enemy ships is ground combat on sea. It can overwhelm you but can be cheesed.
7/10
Building:
Building is awesome. Making structures, bases, rugs, lamps, all the things, so fun. Easy to learn and challenging to master. If they add more to this part of the game they could have a Minecraft level of fun. As it is the majority of hours I have in the game are all building things. If you like this kind of thing you will LOVE this.
9/10
Overall experience:
7.5/10
Buy it!

I have 155 Hours so far and still feels Fun and Refreshing and a blast! the story is intresting and the side quests are fun and the characters are all diffrent and have a purpose, Time fly's when having fun and Time in this game is always fun weather you want to Sail Adventure Fight Craft Collect resourses, farm or grind for levels or the story or for better gear. I like that the game tempers it's tactical gameplay so that it never feels like a chore to sail and fight at sea. 

There are no worries about wind direction hampering your ability to get from one place to another as it doesn't exist in the model. Instead there is a waypoint system that makes it a snap to get to most of your objectives without the need for super ;ong voyages. However, you are limited to creating ten waypoints of your own, so you can't simply pepper the map with them. But when combined with the pre-existing waypoints set up at faction owned islands, ten should be more than enough.

Ship-to-ship combat is straightforward with positioning being the most important element. Reacting quickly to your opponent's course changes so you can get immediately get fresh guns to fire is key to success. Especially against higher level enemies who can deplete half your hull with a single broadside. 

There are also boarding actions where you climb aboard a crippled enemy vessel with your crew and fight hand-to-hand against the enemy crew. The rewards for doing this vary only slightly and unless you are boarding a transport vessel, it's really not woth the effort. You will never find rare or special loot after a successful boarding action, just coin, repair kits and insignias with which you can earn the favor of the various factions you encounter.

The land based combat is likewise fairly simplistic without a lot of intricacy that needs to be mastered. Outside of specific circumstances, combat consists of strikes, heavy strikes, dodging and parrying. I found this enjoyable enough, but others may crave more depth.

You can hire workers for your base that give you slight improvements to different production tasks. For instance, there is a worker who will generate extra dishes for you each time you cook. This is what I wanted Sea of Thieves to be.

A cool pirate game that's co-op without the requirement of having PVP to worry about.  I wanted to set some sails, sea some shanties, and swash some buckles, and this game does all of that without having some randoms/griefers making it their day-job to ruin other people's fun.  It's not perfect, but for an Early Access game, it is very good and has lots of content.

To address a few items in particular:

The Combat.
        It's okay.  I wouldn't call it amazing, but wouldn't call it the worst thing either.  The mechanics are basic here.  Until you get some later items, you're going to be using a light attack and heavy attack pretty much exclusively until around mid-game.  You can find some guns (pistols/muskets/etc.), but your usage will be limited until you later unlock the ability to craft your own gunpowder.  Then it gets to feeling more like fighting as a pirate.  As you upgrade your gear and find better weapons, there's a bit more depth (some items have bleed, some have special actions, etc).

Ships & Sea Battles
        These are great.  Sailing feels good and love that you can toggle on sea shanties to have your crew sing while you're sailing.  They're really good.  It takes some skill early on to take down ships.  Like everything else, there are upgrades that help make things easier and add a little depth, and it feels nice when you've worked hard to get to the point where you can get obliterate others.  The cannon volleys have to be strategic with long cooldowns, and you have to lead the enemy to time it right.  It's a good feeling when you can nail a long distance volley while they're trying to turn around to come back and broadside you with their cannons.  Once you get their health low enough, they're sitting ducks unable to retaliate until you either finish them off or board them.  Boarding the enemy ship is fun and grants extra spoils. claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a waypoint limit, restricting players to creating a maximum of ten personal waypoints on the map.

citations.review_text:
I've had plenty of bad events to post a negative review but if you can handle the grind leveling up you'll gain combat satisfaction. Programs that agitate me with difficulty and hardship keep me burdened with finding solutions and this is one of them.
I've hired an alchemist gal because there's a shortage and she's good at mixing ingredients. I've also just hired a cook because you are what you eat and what you eat changes your combat effectiveness.
There's not enough bars open and no gambling but it is early access and there is still hope.
High sea combat is much like AC Black Flag so I have no problem with that and my new Brigg is just about ready for deployment after the ships equipment is leveled up.
Base building and construction will burn thru lots of time. I just figured out how to keep all that smoke out of my primary base and I've got hideouts all over the place where you cannot place a fast travel bell because they're limited in number.
An overclocked I7-6700K with an rtx2060 is running the program but this does not meet minimum specs. I had crashes but the Nvidia program helped me set what they recommended and it worked.
Your expectations may be satisfied if you can tolerate newbie vulnerability. Level 9 is coming up and this is why I posted this review. My construction has reached epic levels and I'll spend plenty of time upgrading all my other outposts. I'll see ya when I see ya and I'll pour your Rum visiting my home base.

I like that the game tempers it's tactical gameplay so that it never feels like a chore to sail and fight at sea. 

There are no worries about wind direction hampering your ability to get from one place to another as it doesn't exist in the model. Instead there is a waypoint system that makes it a snap to get to most of your objectives without the need for super ;ong voyages. However, you are limited to creating ten waypoints of your own, so you can't simply pepper the map with them. But when combined with the pre-existing waypoints set up at faction owned islands, ten should be more than enough.

Ship-to-ship combat is straightforward with positioning being the most important element. Reacting quickly to your opponent's course changes so you can get immediately get fresh guns to fire is key to success. Especially against higher level enemies who can deplete half your hull with a single broadside. 

There are also boarding actions where you climb aboard a crippled enemy vessel with your crew and fight hand-to-hand against the enemy crew. The rewards for doing this vary only slightly and unless you are boarding a transport vessel, it's really not woth the effort. You will never find rare or special loot after a successful boarding action, just coin, repair kits and insignias with which you can earn the favor of the various factions you encounter.

The land based combat is likewise fairly simplistic without a lot of intricacy that needs to be mastered. Outside of specific circumstances, combat consists of strikes, heavy strikes, dodging and parrying. I found this enjoyable enough, but others may crave more depth.

You can hire workers for your base that give you slight improvements to different production tasks. For instance, there is a worker who will generate extra dishes for you each time you cook. There aren't many of these workers but they are generally worthwhile if you can afford to hire them. Watch out though. They have a tendency to get underfoot an…

claims.claim: Early game land combat features aggressive, high-damage enemies that can quickly kill players if they fail to manage stamina, blocking, or dodging.

citations.review_text:
This game is really fun. There are many comparisons to Valheim. They are not unwarranted. The progression methods by biomes, crafting and building, sea travel, very much along the same lines. The graphics are superior, many quality of life improvements. Progression is easier and quicker, dying is not as punishing. I have spent most of my time building, as i did in Valheim and 7 Days to Die.
Combat took a minute to get a handle on. You must dodge or block, not Chad. The builds are coming along, but not quite as polished as I hope they will be. I enjoy single player, it is tough, but you can make it easier in the settings. Really fun with friends. They abandoned the free to play, pay to win model they were originally considering, and it is the best decision ever made for this game. Yall need to quit funneling money into those games, your just encouraging them.

Super fun & awesome game ruined entirely by the combat & balance. Mostly a numbers issue. Every source of bonus damage is genuinely so small it's not ever worth getting or investing in instead of more stamina and health, and enemies constantly swarm you, two shot you, and are incredibly tanky on normal difficulty. You are as well forced to fight these enemies to get the materials you need to upgrade your gear to their level so that you can bypass the insane damage reduction they get from being higher level than your gear. Enemies also get hyper armor to interrupt your combos, but they also get it seemingly at random just to ruin your day even more.

Naval combat is also about as bad. When you want to sail to a new area for new resources and new gear, including a new ship & gear for that, you will have to sail around all of the groups of enemy ships spawning in your way, otherwise they will effectively one shot you, since your ship is too weak until you get the materials to make a new one that they are guarding. Enemy ships also have pretty high aggro range, and are much faster & more maneuverable than your ships of the same type.

There are two main parts to this game. The game, hacking, slashing, shooting, quests, ship combat, and the building.

The game:
Ground combat feels janky at first then you get the rhythm down. Then it becomes a dance. Know how your character moves and learn the enemies. Then you have it. The builds are varied but you get few points so you have to really choose one fighting style or another and stick to it. More than two enemies on you early in the game is likely a death.
6/10
Ship Combat:
The basic combat is great. Floating around and blasting enemies is a true joy. The build variety for your ship is basic but gives you some choice on how to play. Fast and pew or slower and tankier. 
Boarding enemy ships is ground combat on sea. It can overwhelm you but can be cheesed.
7/10
Building:
Building is awesome. Making structures, bases, rugs, lamps, all the things, so fun. Easy to learn and challenging to master. If they add more to this part of the game they could have a Minecraft level of fun. As it is the majority of hours I have in the game are all building things. If you like this kind of thing you will LOVE this.
9/10
Overall experience:
7.5/10
Buy it!

Very fun Game and i am inlove with the building mechanics and how cheap the materials are, the early game was very punishing, but realizing weapons damage scale with leveling and needs to be the same level with the mobs to do 100% damage, quickly changed the issue. The quests are pretty lack luster but following them gave me motivation to explore. Being a early access game i wont go to into detail about some holes that are missing in thegame as i believe many will be addressed in upcoming updates.

My wife and I just finished conquering everything this early access game currently offers, and let me tell you, nothing bonds a marriage like getting absolutely obliterated by Dodos. These things hit like they’ve been training at CrossFit Pirate Bay.

Normal mode? Yeah, “Normal.” Sure. In the beginning we were basically two underdressed tourists being mugged by prehistoric chickens. But once you start finding gear you actually care about and upgrading it, suddenly you go from “Please don’t hurt me” to “I am the captain now.”

The pirate vibes are immaculate. At one point I caught myself saying “Yarr” unironically, which is a cry for help but also a sign the game is doing something right. The building system is shockingly good too — simple at first, then suddenly you’re unlocking new tiles and patterns like some kind of nautical IKEA wizard.

If you like pirates and survival games, this thing won’t disappoint. It’s worth every penny, especially if you enjoy yelling “WHY IS THE DODO SO STRONG!” with someone you love. We had a blast and can’t wait for more content.

Windrose is a genuinely enjoyable survival-adventure game, up to the end of the Foothills content at least. For a Single Player experience, the first two biomes deliver a well-paced loop of exploration, crafting, and naval combat that kept me engaged throughout. The problem is that the game's quality drops noticeably the moment you reach the Cursed Swamp, and what was a fun experience starts feeling like a chore. For that reason, I'd rate this a solid 7/10 with the expectation that the developers address these issues before full release. I'll list the improvement points from my opinion:

- Character progression is limited. The RPG tag is misleading; it merely has elements of it but it's not RPG. A real RPG lets you build a character around your preferred playstyle, the game accommodates you, and Windrose doesn't. Enemy encounters, particularly in the later biome, demand optimal play: you parry or dodge, or you die when you run out of stamina. The stat and talent system exists, but it functions more as a modifier layer on top of your gear than a genuine identity-defining system. You're not building a character but configuring one. That's a survival game design, not RPG.

- Sailing is one of Windrose's highlights, and naval combat is fun, at least for the first few encounters. The problem is enemy spawn rates. After a naval battle, another enemy ship spawns almost immediately, sometimes directly in your path. This cycle repeating seven times in a single stretch stops being exciting and becomes tedious. A spawn rate adjustment, or at minimum preventing enemies from spawning directly in front of your course, would go a long way.
Boarding actions compound this. Clearing 20 enemies on a Frigate is engaging the first time. By the fourth or fifth boarding, it wears thin. Some tuning on enemy density during boarding would help the combat retain its appeal longer.
Ship variety also has a balance problem. The Blackbeard variant is functionally the only viable choice if you wan…

Absolutely amazing game, ship battles are intense, difficulty is hard. Highly recommend but dont expect to play anything else for the first few weeks, addicting...! end level tip - Stack your stamina, its the most important trait!

I'm rooting for this game and will absolutely change my review if these pain points are fixed.
Game has a ton of potential but the combat balance is terrible.    You can change the difficulty setting to match your taste but most people are going to start with what is labeled as the "Intended Windrose Experience" and have a terrible time to be honest.  Clunky combat is fine for a game like this,  I would point to Valhiem as an example of clunky combat that's balanced accordingly, but this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Its clunky as ♥♥♥♥,  you get 2 shot on the normal difficulty even with upgraded armor and they throw multiple enemies at you over and over.  I'm sorry but I don't want to resort to building cheese to fight through the game.  Ship combat is ok, still unbalanced but ♥♥♥♥ really hits the fan when you try and board enemy ships.  Have fun fighting in a restricted area, getting 2 shot by enemies that take 4 or 5 hits to kill and while swinging a halberd through their heads and not hitting followed by a 5 minute sail back to start all over again.   Completely breaks the immersion and sense of adventure that these survival crafting games should impart.

Do you like Valheim, 7 Days 2 Die? AC Black Flag? Base building and exploring? Then this is the game for you!

Windrose is awesome, plain and simple. And not just "awesome for a EA game", because this is much more than that. With right over 100 hours in-game, I've encountered minimal bugs, glitches or exploits. The game is polished, has a great building system that would make both Valheim and 7D2D envious. Lots of different building options and styles. And the best part? Building doesnt necessarily cost a ton of materials! 

The game features (currently) 3 different biomes, all 3 quite different for each other with different materials, enemies and POIs. Well, 4 biomes if you count the Ocean. Theres loads to explore in each biome, making each fun and new, requiring different tactics for defeating the new enemies. The POIs are great! I love the puzzles and the hidden loot you have to search for. And they are quite diverse for a EA game.

Windrose has a lot of different weapon and armor options, suited for what ever style of combat you prefer. I would say however, that the game is melee focused. I at least, couldnt make ranged only combat work for me.

Im really looking forward to future updates!

Now, for the "negative parts". And I really dont see them as negative just yet, seeing as its still in EA and theres still loads to come. So, rather than "negative", lets call it "Stuff I feel the game needs":

The quest progression makes the game quite linear, if you let it. I personally prefer to explore on my own rather than follow markers on a map. And I did so here a well, searching out and exploring every single island. So, rather than a quest being marked on a map, I'd love to see it more general. "Find the island shaped like a horse shoe", "Search east of Tortuga for the ship your hunting" and so on.

Ahoy matey!
Kraken Express does a great job balancing the many aspects of open-world survival gaming. The story and varied biomes that continue to flow throughout the island chain act like soft levels without creating inaccessible areas. Overall, the enemies are well balanced, and combat requires timing and experience without being punishingly difficult. Tactics matter, and all the skills, stats, and upgrades make sense within the world.
The inclusion of the Spanish conquistadors was a great touch. Their embrace of making the game about discovery through the varied environmental conditions reflect the same care found in the lore, story development, and attention to the time period. The world is engaging enough that it almost made me forget the tyranny of colonization. 
The balance of how players can acquire the ingredients they need is well laddered to the  biomes and with enough options to encourage being at sea as much as on land.
I played through the game with a friend on our own server, and we had just finished the last boss. As we walked back to our boats, he said, "Now we can focus on gathering resources for Ashlands." That's probably the highest compliment we can give a game.
It scratches many of the same exploration, progression, and cooperative survival itches without feeling like it's simply just a copy of another game ( i did play SOT but it hit differently).
All that being said, the art—particularly the heads, bodies, and clothes—does seem to be one of the weaker points. Unlike the jewelry, which changes appearance as it levels up, the clothing seems locked into a single look. The character sculpts and outfits don't feel entirely fleshed out (excuse the pun), and some of the more awkward motions, like jumping or transitioning into and out of actions such as reloading, stand out next to the otherwise polished experience.
The overall look and feel of the characters almost needs more stylization. The world itself strikes a hard-fought balance between styliz…
